claims.proposition: GitButler snapshots selected native/worktree state; its undo promise does not establish complete repository or historical backup.

evidence.exact_quote: **Reconciled conclusion.** The architecture in the handoff is supported. GitButler records operation-scoped native recovery state, with explicit exclusions and compatibility behavior. “Unlimited undo” is not evidence of complete repository, worktree or historical backup. The suggested untracked-file size exclusion is contradicted by the implementation at the handoff pin.

- [Timeline documentation](https://docs.gitbutler.com/features/timeline), S00001:30–39: “Undo nearly any of your actions”; before major actions it snapshots virtual branches, uncommitted work and conflicts in the Git object database; “Revert” restores the pre-action state. It also “Occasionally” snapshots recently changed uncommitted files. This supports automatic pre-action recovery and occasional dirty-file capture, without proving continuous capture or every operation's coverage. The [README](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/8861f862414df646220fc6f935b4ab404456d577/README.md#L59-L74), S00015:59–74, uses broader “unlimited undo” and “all operations” wording.
- [Pinned oplog implementation](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/8861f862414df646220fc6f935b4ab404456d577/crates/gitbutler-oplog/src/oplog.rs#L782-L962), S00010:782–962: the implementation records index and optional index-conflict trees, target tree, conflict sidecars, selected project metadata, branch order, virtual-branch metadata/trees/commit bytes, and the worktree. It additionally records ad-hoc checkout identity, an optional extra reference and the workspace commit independently of HEAD. `project_meta.toml` means selected target reference/commit and push-remote fields (44–51), **not the entire project database**. Capture derives projected workspace metadata, overlays it through `set_workspace`, synchronizes applied-stack heads from refs and serializes it; it is not just a copy of a potentially stale TOML file (860–928). The acquired-head oplog file S00035 is byte-identical to S00010.
- [Linked-worktree API](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/8861f862414df646220fc6f935b4ab404456d577/crates/but-api/src/worktrees.rs#L5-L10), S00011:5–10: these experimental operations are feature-gated, and “None of the mutations here take part in the oplog: archived state is a project-database row, and a removed checkout cannot be restored from a snapshot.” The database and removed-checkout limits are explicit, rather than inferred from missing documentation.

The [oplog implementation at 8861f86](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/8861f862414df646220fc6f935b4ab404456d577/crates/gitbutler-oplog/src/oplog.rs#L782-L962) records selected state, including target, branch-order, index/conflict and workspace data (S00010). The [capture implementation](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/8861f862414df646220fc6f935b4ab404456d577/crates/but-core/src/repo_ext.rs#L219-L376) disables its size filter when the limit is zero, omits ignored/pruned directory entries, and handles submodules as commit entries rather than recursively capturing dirty submodule contents (S00033). The [worktree API](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/8861f862414df646220fc6f935b4ab404456d577/crates/but-api/src/worktrees.rs#L5-L10) excludes archive/remove from oplog (S00011).

claims.proposition: Snapshot preparation, publication and GC-retention updates are separate stages; deliberately maintained reflogs are retention roots.

evidence.exact_quote: - **Preparation and publication differ:** S00010:142–159 says the prepared tree is undiscoverable until committed. The implementation writes the snapshot commit, updates oplog-head state, and then updates retention references (965–1002). [Retention code](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/079f2d998fc3e2d882f68c5f535d101272ed28cf/crates/gitbutler-oplog/src/reflog.rs#L37-L99), S00040, deliberately maintains `gitbutler/target` reflog entries protecting target, oplog and last-pushed-base commits from GC. This is positive retention evidence, but those sequential writes are not proof of crash-atomic publication, and a visible branch listing alone does not describe the retention roots.

[Snapshot publication](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/8861f862414df646220fc6f935b4ab404456d577/crates/gitbutler-oplog/src/oplog.rs#L965-L1002) creates a commit, writes the oplog head, then updates retention references (S00010). [Retention code](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/079f2d998fc3e2d882f68c5f535d101272ed28cf/crates/gitbutler-oplog/src/reflog.rs#L37-L99) maintains a synthetic `gitbutler/target` reflog linking target, oplog and last-pushed-base commits (S00040). This is positive evidence of deliberate GC protection, not proof that copying a visible branch or printing the timeline preserves it.

evidence.exact_quote: - [July 23 independent comment](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/issues/14848#issuecomment-5063257903), S00003, reports 168 upstream-changed files, **153 previously clean files left with older committed contents**, and worktree/base divergence increasing from 19 to 183 files while base/HEAD advanced. It explicitly says “related outcome, not proof of the same code path,” reports no loud error, and cannot isolate the gating conditions. Its intact snapshot chain is useful reported evidence; the raw per-file artifacts were not independently obtained. The claimed deterministic core, skipped-checkout explanation and exclusion of a race are not established merely by before/after snapshots. Also correct its detection heuristic: matching an ancestor's bytes alone does not distinguish stale content from an intentional user revert; a known clean baseline is necessary.

The [July 23 comment](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/issues/14848#issuecomment-5063257903) describes GitButler 0.21.0, a dirty worktree and a base advance affecting 168 files, with 153 previously clean files retaining older committed bytes while HEAD/base advanced. It reports snapshot divergence increasing from 19 to 183 files and an unchanged example-file mtime (S00003). These counts are the reporter's measurements; the private repository and raw per-file artifacts were not independently examined.

Independent direction: preserve a controlled before/after manifest separating genuinely dirty paths, applied-stack paths and initially clean base-only paths. Advance only upstream content, then compare each class against expected committed and worktree blobs and index stages. Vary dirty-file presence, stack count, concurrent external writers and stack removal independently.

The reporter explicitly says the outcome is not proof of the loud assertion path. Their claim of a deterministic core and a skipped checkout is an inference; snapshots around an operation do not alone prove absence of a race. Their heuristic that an ancestor-matching dirty blob must be stale is also insufficient by itself: a user can intentionally revert a file to an ancestor's content. Baseline provenance is necessary before classifying or discarding changes.

Alternative explanations include skipped/failed checkout, legitimate local edits, projection changes or an external writer. Keep this direction independent from both assertion failures and stack eviction; preserve the parent aggregate's uncertain disposition.

The patch changes future metadata construction; it does not rewrite historical snapshot bytes. Thus a completed restore with a correctly captured and published before-state can support redo; preparation alone, an interrupted restore, a publication failure or an already uncapturable current state does not prove an available redo entry. Restore also logs and ignores conflict-sidecar errors (1053–1055) and ignores individual applied-head ref-write errors with `.ok()` (1189). Those are code-derived reasons for independently checking the restored state, not locally reproduced failures.

**Preserved lesson, alternatives and remaining questions.** Compare graph, stack-scoped ownership, captured metadata and actual restored refs/objects independently; a correct graph or valid serialization can hide the wrong ownership. Preserve legitimate shared segments rather than deleting all duplicate names. Existing generic restore tests in S00045 add narrower positive evidence, including missing-commit reconstitution and malformed-format rejection; they do not establish full historical ownership recovery. Alternatives include rejecting semantically inconsistent metadata before mutation and exposing a bounded recovery procedure when an old capture cannot satisfy those invariants. No automatic repair of old captures or universal redo guarantee is claimed.

[#15573](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/issues/15573) reports an eight-segment restore rewinding only the top ref. [#15584](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/pull/15584) says it prevents newly degraded metadata but does not repair snapshots already recorded; fresh before-restore capture should make a bad historical restore recoverable with redo (S00007/S00005).
